# Dissections

::: {.doc-lead}
Keep the supporting panels, statistics and notes one step away from the main plot.
:::

A figure panel is a verdict: *caloric intake predicts body weight*. The evidence behind that
verdict — twenty per-subject curves, the model comparison you didn't show, the ANOVA table —
usually lives in a scratch folder far from the figure, or nowhere at all. **Dissections** give
that material a home *attached to the plot itself*: a folder beside the plot that Flux shows
live in the sidebar while you compose, opens full-screen on **D**, and searches by note.

The quickest start: with a figure open, press **Alt+G** to show the **Plots** view, click a
plot, and read its **Dissections** in the lower pane. Press **+ Note** there to write the first
note. Everything else on this page explains what the pane shows and how to fill it from your
analysis script.

## The folder convention {#the-folder-convention}

Any plot in `plots/` can own a dissection folder named after it under `plots/_dissections/`:

```
plots/
├── growth.svg                      # the composed panel
└── _dissections/
    └── growth/                     # ← growth.svg's dissections
        ├── overview.svg            #   loose files form the default group
        ├── notes.txt               #   a note: plain text, searchable
        ├── by_subject/             #   a subfolder is a named group (a section in the viewer)
        │   ├── subj01.svg …
        └── _stats/
            └── anova.csv           #   CSVs/TSVs open as sortable tables
```

The name mirrors the plot's path under `plots/` (so `plots/models/fit.svg` owns
`plots/_dissections/models/fit/`), with the extension dropped. Pasted images and PDF snips
work too — they're keyed by their file name.

That's the whole contract. There is no manifest and no registration: **the folder is the
API**. Your analysis script (or an agent) drops files in. Flux can create a dissection folder
and write the text notes you edit there; it leaves your images, tables and other files alone.

## What goes in {#what-goes-in}

Anything that explains the plot. Typical dissections:

- **Breakdowns** — one panel per subject / session / condition behind a summary plot.
- **Alternative analyses** — the same question answered another way (different model,
  different normalisation), kept honest next to the version you published.
- **Statistics** — `_stats/` CSVs with the tests behind the asterisks. The
  [`fp.stats`](/docs/statistics.html) functions return rows made to be saved there.
- **Notes** — one or more `.txt` files with observations, decisions and searchable tags such
  as `#check`.
- Images of any kind (**svg**, **png**, **jpg**, **webp** — fluxplot outputs included) and
  **csv**/**tsv** tables are first-class in the viewer; `.txt` notes open in the note editor;
  other files are listed by name.

Dissections are deliberately **out of the way of composition**: nothing under `_dissections/`
turns up in an ordinary plot search, lands in a figure by accident, or rides along into an
export. They are context, not content.

Out of the way is not locked away. In the Plots rail's search box or the full
[Plot gallery](/docs/plot-gallery.html#search-and-insert), type **`_`** and the reserved folders
(`_dissections`, and `_lighttable` if the project has one) appear as rows you can enter with
**Enter**. Inside one, searching only looks *within* that folder, so you can find a
per-subject panel and insert it deliberately — **Backspace** in an empty search steps back
out to the ordinary `plots/` search. In the Dissections pane itself, you can also drag a
panel straight onto a figure.

## Viewing them {#viewing-them}

**Beside the canvas, live.** The sidebar's **Plots** view (**Alt+G**; it also opens a hidden
sidebar, and **Alt+G** again returns to **Layers**) has the plot gallery on top and the
**Dissections** of whichever plot you last clicked below — a plot clicked in the gallery or on
the canvas — and follows each new click. Tables come first as small previews (a one-row
statistics table reads as a list), then each folder of panels; very large folders show a few
and **Show all**. Clicking a placed per-subject panel shows its siblings, the folder it came
from. With a file selected, clicking another plot that has a file of the same name keeps it
selected in the same place, so you can flip between plots and compare one subject. Clicking an
empty spot keeps the last plot showing; the **pin** holds the pane on one plot while you work
elsewhere. **Double-click**, **Enter** or **Space** opens a file in the full viewer. Drag the
line between gallery and dissections to share the height, drag it to an edge to fold a part
away, and double-click it to reset. A tile's **⧉ 12** mark means the plot has 12 dissection
files; click it to show them. Slides have the same rail beside the slide list.

<figure class="doc-figure"><a href="/assets/media/docs/figure-plots-rail.png" data-enlarge data-caption="Click a plot and its dissections appear below the gallery: tables first as small previews, then each folder of panels. The folder shown here is illustrative."><img src="/assets/media/docs/figure-plots-rail.png" alt="The Figure workspace with the sidebar in its Plots view: a gallery of plot tiles under folder headings, and below it a Dissections pane listing a summary table and a folder of panels for the selected plot." width="2800" height="2000" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Click a plot and its dissections appear below the gallery: tables first as small previews, then each folder of panels. The folder shown here is illustrative.</figcaption></figure>

**Full screen.** In the Figure workspace, select a plot and press **D** (or click
**Dissections** in the Inspector — it shows a count). The viewer opens full-screen, and the
**⧉** button shrinks it to a floating window you can keep beside the canvas. It is the rail's
pane at full size: tables first as Summary previews, then each folder of panels as its own
section at the panels' own shapes, then the remaining files as a list.

| Key | In the full viewer |
|---|---|
| **Arrow keys** | move through the files |
| **\[** / **\]** or **Ctrl+scroll** | make the tiles smaller or larger |
| **1–9** | jump to a section; a section's ▾ folds it |
| **Enter** | expand a file; on an image, toggle fit / 1:1 |
| **Ctrl+scroll**, **Space+drag** or plain scroll | zoom an image at the cursor, pan it |
| **Esc** | step back: detail → grid → closed |

CSV/TSV files open as tables with a sticky header — click a column to sort, numeric columns
right-align. The viewer is live: files dropped into the folder while it's open simply appear.

Plot previews use the same readable background in the sidebar, Space preview, full gallery
and this viewer: each image sits on its own page, transparent dark text on paper, light text
on a dark surface. An image's own background remains part of the image.

## Notes and finding plots {#notes-and-finding-plots}

### Write notes {#notes}

In the sidebar's Dissections pane, switch from **Files** to **✎ Notes**, or click **✎ Notes**
in the full viewer, then **+ Note** to create a text file. Give each note a name; Flux adds
`.txt` if needed, and a plot can have several named notes. Select a file to edit it;
double-clicking a `.txt` among a plot's files opens it here too. Notes save as you type and
when you leave the field; **Ctrl+S** saves immediately. A failed save keeps your draft, and an
external edit is reported instead of being overwritten. The text files remain readable in any
editor, and your scripts can write them too.

<figure class="doc-figure doc-figure-compact"><a href="/assets/media/docs/figure-dissections-notes.png" data-enlarge data-caption="Notes are plain text files beside the plot’s dissections. They save as you type; tags such as #check are searchable across the project."><img src="/assets/media/docs/figure-dissections-notes.png" alt="The Plots view with the Dissections pane switched to Notes: a file tab named observations.txt, a + Note button and the note text being edited, with a #check tag in it." width="638" height="1746" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Notes are plain text files beside the plot’s dissections. They save as you type; tags such as <code>#check</code> are searchable across the project.</figcaption></figure>

### Search notes {#search-notes}

In the Plots rail's search, turn on **Notes** to search note contents across every plot in the
project. For example, `#check` finds that tag wherever you wrote it. Each result shows the
plot, note, line and the matching text; click it to select that plot and open the note in the
Notes pane below. Switch **Notes** off to return to searching plot names.

### Browse by folder {#folder-tree}

To browse folders, click **Folders** in the Dissections pane or press **Alt+/** (from anywhere
in Figure or Slide; it opens the Plots view if needed). The lower pane becomes a searchable
folder tree with the number of plots under each folder. Click a folder (or use the **Arrow
keys** and **Enter**) to show only its plots; choose the top folder to see everything again.
Press **Alt+/** again, or **Esc**, to restore Dissections. The chosen folder stays in place
while you switch the sidebar to Layers and back. Companion collections such as `_dissections`
stay out of this tree.

### From the command line {#command-line}

For scripts and agents, `flux list-dissections [plot]` prints a plot's groups and files (or,
with no argument, every plot that has dissections); writing needs no verb — drop files in the
folder. See the [command reference](/docs/commands.html#verb-reference).

## Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

| Symptom | Cause → fix |
|---|---|
| Pressed **D** and got "select a plot" | Dissect works on a selected plot or image (or a drilled part; the part's owning plot is used; with several selected, the last plot you added). Group selections don't map to one dissection folder → select one plot. |
| The Plots view says **Library plots have no dissections** | Plots from your global plot library live outside the project; dissections belong to a project's `plots/_dissections` → place the plot in the project, or keep its evidence with the project it is used in. |
| The viewer says the folder doesn't exist | Nothing has created it yet → the empty state's **Create dissection folder** button does it, and shows the exact path. |
| Renamed a plot and its dissections vanished | Flux never renames files in `plots/` → rename the matching folder under `plots/_dissections/` yourself. Until you do, the plot reports no dissections; nothing breaks and the folder is never deleted. |
| A file shows as a name card with no preview | Images and CSV/TSV files have previews; `.txt` notes open in the text editor → other files remain listed by name so you know they're there. |
| A note won't save | Text notes are limited to 1 MiB and cannot follow symbolic links → shorten the note or keep large text elsewhere. If another editor changed the file, copy any draft text you want to keep, then choose **Discard draft and reload** to read the disk version before editing again. |
